The number of phonemic tone levels in the other dialects has not been fully analyzed, but based on current data there are possibly only three. 5508.idn: Name in the source: Pyen; family in the source: Bisoid subgroup of the Southern Ngwi branch, Tibeto-Burman

tn.quote: Pyen has three contrastive tones, high, mid, and low, with stop-final syllables taking only mid and low tones. The low tone has falling pitch, the other tones are fairly level. Verb stems and nouns carry all three tones; the majority of these must take the mid-tone prefix /āŋ-/ … Suffixes have either high or low tone, but for at least three verb suffixes the tone is unspecified. These are the markers /-ne/ ‘imperfective’, /-ɟi/ ‘cited form’, and /-kʲa/ ‘place.where’, occurring with both high or low tone since their realization depends on the tone of the preceding verb stem or suffix.
tn.cite: Hornéy, Christina Scotte. 2019. Tonal Variation in Pyen. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society (JSEALS) 12(1): 12-24. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. http://hdl.handle.net/10524/52442

tn.note: Three contrastive tones, high, mid and low (low slightly falling), on stems and nouns; stop-final syllables take only mid or low; three toneless verb suffixes are high after high/mid, low after low.

tn.quote: 3.2. Tones Like other Tibeto-Burman languages, Reang is a tone language in which a change in the pitch of the syllable corresponds to a change in its meaning. Reang has two lexical tones namely high and low. (i) Low: the tension of the vocal cords in the production of a syllable is relatively low, causing a low pitch. The low tone is marked by the symbol / ˋ/. (ii) High: the tension of the vocal cords in the production of a syllable is relatively high, causing a high pitch. It is represented by the symbol / ʹ/. … ̸ kəˋtúŋ̸ „wool‟ ̸ kəˋtùŋ ̸ „hot‟ ̸ hór ̸ „fire‟ ̸ hòr ̸ „night‟ …

tn.note: Two lexical tones, high and low, marked with acute and grave; a change in the pitch of a syllable changes meaning (e.g. hór 'fire' vs hòr 'night'). Nothing is said about word stress.

tn.quote: Sur le plan tonal, le seki manifeste trois (3) tonèmes selon M. E. Gningah (2010, p. 142), à savoir: un tonème /H/ et un tonème /B/ respectivement représenté par / ʹ/ et / ˋ/. Mais aussi, un tonème descendant /D/ noté /^/. Les tonèmes ont une fonction distinctive dans la langue. … les deux tons, H et B, apparaissent dans toutes les positions (initiale, médiane, finale) … Le tonème descendant quant à lui a été répertorié exclusivement en position finale des dissyllabiques /mbándzâ/ « bambou » ou dans les monosyllabiques /mbô/ « plante du pied ».
tn.translation: On the tonal level, Seki shows three (3) tonemes according to M. E. Gningah (2010, p. 142), namely a /H/ toneme and a /L/ toneme written with acute and grave respectively, and also a falling toneme /D/ written /^/. The tonemes have a distinctive function in the language. … the two tones H and L appear in all positions (initial, medial, final) … The falling toneme has been recorded only in final position of disyllables /mbándzâ/ 'bamboo' or in monosyllables /mbô/ 'sole of the foot'.
tn.cite: Koumbi Mabiti, Glenn Aymar. 2025. Phonologie diachronique des parlers du groupe Kota-Kele (B20) pour un affinement des embranchements internes. Thèse de doctorat, Université Omar Bongo (Libreville), dir. Y. Nzang Bie. 381 pp. HAL tel-04957912.

tn.quote: Tai Nuea has nine tones: six unchecked and three checked. Among the unchecked tones, there are two level tones: a mid-level tone (T33) and a high-level tone (T55). … Additionally, there are two falling tones: a mid-falling tone (T31) and a high-falling tone (T51). … There are also two rising tones, T24 and T35. … There are three checked tones in Tai Nuea. tones: tweetoppig accent (two-peaked long vowel, marked ^ over the vowel; not a counted toneme: § 397 treats hard/háld as two vowel phonemes ɔ:/a: merging into one)
tn.quote: Opm. Oudere Terschellingers maken verschil tussen a: in [hs:t] hard en de tweetoppige vocaal a: in [hs<:'t] haard. … < > boven vocaal duidt tweetoppig accent aan. … § 381. In tegenstelling tot het ndl. … is de lang-kort-correlatie in 't fri.-tersch. primair. … § 397. … Daar de genoemde twee woorden de enige zijn, waarin a: en a: nog verschillende phonemen zijn en dit verschil door de tegenwoordige dialectsprekers niet meer in acht genomen wordt, … mogen we constateren, dat 9: en a:, voorzover ze niet zijn samengevallen, phonetische realisaties van één phoneem zijn.
tn.translation: Note. Older Terschellingers distinguish ɔ: in [hɔ:t] 'hard' from the two-peaked vowel ɔ̂: in [hɔ̂:t] 'hâld (holds)' [scan 'haard'; phonetic symbols scan-garbled]. … ^ over a vowel marks two-peaked accent. … § 381. In contrast to Dutch … in Terschelling Frisian the long-short correlation is primary. … § 397. … Since the two words mentioned are the only ones in which ɔ: and ɔ̂: are still different phonemes, and present-day dialect speakers no longer observe this difference, … we may conclude that ɔ: and ɔ̂:, insofar as they have not merged, are phonetic realisations of one phoneme.

tn.quote: On relève en tikar des tons ponctuels cl des Ions modulés. … Au niveau phonétique, le tikar connaîl trois tons ponctuels: haut, moyen, bas. … Donc, au niveau morphotonologique, l'opposition trinairc haut/moycn/bas est réductible à une opposition binaire bas/non-bas. … Quant aux tons modulés, sur le plan phonétique, il y en a quatre: haut-bas, moyen bas, bas haut et bas-moyen. … sur le plan morphotonologique, il y a lieu de ne distinguer que deux Ions modulés, à savoir: un ton non-bas qui descend à un ton bas et un ton bas qui monte à un ton non-bas.
tn.translation: Tikar has level tones and contour tones. … At the phonetic level Tikar has three level tones: high, mid, low. … So at the morphotonological level the three-way high/mid/low opposition is reducible to a binary low/non-low opposition. … As for the contour tones, phonetically there are four: high-low, mid-low, low-high and low-mid. … at the morphotonological level only two contour tones need be distinguished, namely a non-low tone that falls to a low tone and a low tone that rises to a non-low tone.
tn.cite: Stanley, Carol. 1991. Description morpho-syntaxique de la langue tikar (parlée au Cameroun). Épinay-sur-Seine / Yaoundé: Société Internationale de Linguistique (SIL). 581 pp. ISBN 2-87751-003-4.

tn.note: Phonetic high, mid, low reduce to low vs non-low (mid predictable by noun class); two contour tones, falling and rising, on about 3% of the lexicon; downdrift in high-low-high; stress not described. tn.quote: Cambap has three level tones, High (H), Mid (M) and Low (L). In citation forms one normally finds one tone per syllable; contours are also attested, though on monosyllables they are rare. Contours are readily analyzable as sequences of level tones. That all possible combinations of H, M, and L are attested on both monosyllabic and disyllabic words provides strong evidence for this analysis. … Tone functions both lexically and grammatically, and contours may also come about through the application of grammatical tone (discussed below).

tn.note: Three level tones, High, Mid and Low, one per syllable, all nine two-tone combinations attested; contours are sequences of levels, some from grammatical tone (imperative MHL); stress not discussed.

tn.quote: Vale has two unambiguous tone levels, which I label as High (H) and Low (L). … Hence, all four of the tone patterns typically expected in a two-tone system occur in Vale. … In this view, the “Superhigh” tone is actually a H tone raised via the phonetic process H-Raising … The non-automatic downstep results from the presence of a floating L tone. … If we accept this view, Vale has five underlying tone melodies: L, H, LH, HL, and HLH. … CVV syllables have two moras and the tone bearing unit (TBU) in Vale is the mora.

evidence_works.detail: Book review of Barclay 2008 (A Grammar of Western Dani, Lincom). Reports that the grammar has no discussion of tone or of word/sentence stress, and that its only mention of word stress is a hedged footnote (Barclay 2008 p. 39) offering penultimate stress as a possible explanation of lengthened vowels in class 4 verbs. 106-107: "Neither in the phonological section nor anywhere else in the grammar is there any discussion of suprasegmental features such as tone, whether it is phonemically functional or not, nor of word or sentence stress.... The only mention of word stress is contained in one sentence in a larger footnote as a possible explanation of a lengthened vowel in one verb (''It could be explained by stress assignment to the penultimate syllable, a process which could have caused the lengthened vowels in the class 4 verbs'' (p. 39)." Secondhand and hedged: not a basis for coding; a pointer to check Barclay 2008 p. 39 directly.

Ces langues ne sont pas tonales, contrairement aux langues parlées plus au nord ou plus au sud. Elles comportent toutes un nombre important de phonèmes, et une structure syllabique caractérisée par l'absence de consonnes finales, sauf dans des emprunts récents.

These languages are not tonal, unlike the languages spoken further north or further south. They all have a large number of phonemes, and a syllable structure characterised by the absence of final consonants, except in recent loanwords.

tn.quote: Le xwela présente deux tons phonologiques: ce sont le tonème H et le tonème B qui ont différentes réalisations. Le tonème H se réalise haut sur une syllabe à consonne sourde ou sur une syllabe constituée d‟une voyelle comme ci-après en (1) (1) a. kú [ku] mourir b. /é/ [é] PPS (3ième pers. Sing) Il est réalisé BH sur une syllabe à consonne obstruante voisée. c. /ìví/ [ìvĭ] enfant d. /ìzέ/ [ìzɛ] canari Le tonème B se réalise bas [-`] sur une syllabe constituée de n‟importe quelle consonne de la langue. … Le ton M est une réalisation du tonème /B/: f./òló/ [ōló] “proverbe” /ìnũ/ [ìnũ] “ chose”
tn.translation: Xwela has two phonological tones: the toneme H and the toneme B [low], which have different realisations. The toneme H is realised high on a syllable with a voiceless consonant or on a syllable consisting of a vowel, as in (1): a. kú 'to die', b. /é/ [é] 3sg subject pronoun. It is realised BH [low-high, rising] on a syllable with a voiced obstruent: c. /ìví/ [ìvĭ] 'child', d. /ìzέ/ [ìzɛ] 'water jar'. The toneme B is realised low on a syllable with any consonant of the language. … The M [mid] tone is a realisation of the toneme /B/: f. /òló/ [ōló] 'proverb', /ìnũ/ [ìnũ] 'thing'.
tn.cite: Djanato, Odilon K. Sindeté. 2012. L'expression du temps et de l'aspect en xwelagbe. Mémoire de maîtrise (Sciences du Langage et de la Communication, option Description linguistique), FLASH, Université d'Abomey-Calavi; dir. Coffi Sambiéni. 57 pp. (BU-UAC mémoire no. 365, année 2012-2013.)

5528.idn: Name in the source: Yeyi; family in the source: Bantu (Yeyi R41; 'Bantu Zone R')

tn.quote: The prosodology section of this chapter is quite detailed and mainly concentrates on an acoustically based analysis of Yeyi prosody. Shortly, the author demonstrates that Yeyi is characterized with High Tone (termed as Prosodeme II), Low Tone (Prosodeme I) which are semantically distinct (p. 57) and have grammatical functions (p. 61) as well as Prosodeme iii. I am aware that the issue of Bantu tone needs much attention which the author succeedes to manage. Furthermore, intonation is given in demarcative and expressive grounds.
tn.cite: Lusekelo, Amani. 2009. Review of Frank Seidel 2008, A Grammar of Yeyi. A Bantu Language of Southern Africa (Koeln: Ruediger Koeppe). Afrikanistik online 2009, 1-5. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2009_3531
tn.locator: para. <4>, p. 2 (reviewing Seidel 2008 ch. 2 'prosodology', pp. 54-99, tone contrast p. 57, grammatical tone p. 61)
tn.note: Two tones, High and Low, lexically and grammatically contrastive (per a review of Seidel's 2008 grammar, whose analysis is acoustic); a third 'Prosodeme III' is named but not described.

5529.idn: Name in the source: Yoy; family in the source: Tai-Kadai language family; branch 'not yet been determined': Ethnologue (Simons & Fennig 2015) Northern branch, 'the same branch as Saek, Tai Mean and Zhuang'; Pitiyawat (2009) Southwestern Tai-Kadai branch (with Thai, Lao, Shan, Black Tai)

tn.quote: In conclusion, Yoy has five phonologically distinctive tones serving to distinguish between lexical items. The five tones of Yoy include mid-leveled tone (tone 1), high-rising tone (tone 2), mid-rising tone (tone 3), mid-falling tone (tone 4), and low-falling creaky tone (tone 5). Please note that all categories of words in Yoy can carry all tones. … Checked syllables in Yoy can carry only tone 1 (mid-leveled tone), tone 2 (high-rising tone), and tone 5 (low-falling creaky).
tn.cite: Phakkahn, Naiyapak. 2017. Phonology and Grammar Sketch of Yoy. MA thesis, California State University, Long Beach.
tn.locator: p. 33, section 2.4 Tone and p. 39, section 2.5.1 Checked Syllables
tn.note: Five tones: mid level, high rising, mid rising, mid falling, low falling creaky (glottal constriction); every syllable carries a tone; checked syllables take only tones 1, 2 and 5; Praat pitch tracks.

5530.loc: pp. 914-915, section 'E. Tonologie Dzâmba', items a-e; type list 'E. La tonologie type Dzamba' p. 901
5530.idn: Name in the source: Dzâmba; family in the source: parlers bantous (Bantu lects of the north-west of the Belgian Congo)

tn.quote: E. T o n o l o g i e Dzâmba. Il y a quelques groupes de parlers dans l’extrême ouest de la région étudiée, entre la Ngiri et l’Ubangi, qui ont une tonologie entièrement différente. Comme elle est, dans cette région, l’apanage des parlers Dzâmba, nous l’avons dénommée: la tonologie Dzâmba. … b. Les préfixes nominaux y ont toujours le ton haut. … à. La tonologie possède des tons doubles courts qui n’ont qu’une valeur tonétique … e. Enfin on a l’impression que la distance entre les tons hauts et bas est moindre …
tn.translation: E. Dzamba tonology. There are a few groups of lects in the far west of the region studied, between the Ngiri and the Ubangi, which have an entirely different tonology. Since in this region it is the preserve of the Dzamba lects, we have named it the Dzamba tonology. ... b. Noun prefixes there always have high tone. ... d. The tonology has short double tones which have only a tonetic value ... e. Finally one has the impression that the distance between the high and low tones is smaller [than in any other lect of the region; this will have to be checked later with instruments].
tn.cite: De Boeck, L. B. 1951. La tonologie des parlers bantous du nord-ouest du Congo belge. Bulletin des Séances de l'Institut Royal Colonial Belge 22(4): 900-919.
tn.locator: pp. 914-915, section 'E. Tonologie Dzâmba', items a-e; type list 'E. La tonologie type Dzamba' p. 901
tn.note: Two tone levels, high and low (noun prefixes always high); short rising/falling tones occur but are called merely phonetic; the high-low interval seems narrow. Survey notes, no full inventory given.

5531.prule: Stress is fixed and falls on the root-initial (stem-initial) syllable of the word (Otieno 2013, attributing the statement to Kaplan 2007, which does not contain it; inflectional prefixes precede the stem).
5531.quote: Kaplan (2007) points out that Dhopadhola stress is fixed and falls on the root initial syllable of the word. The syllable structure of the language is (C) V (V) (C). … The stressed syllable is underlined; it falls on the stem initial syllable. Dhopadhola like Dholuo has two tones and both are active in the prosodic phonology of the language.
5531.loc: sec. 5.2.6 'An Optimality Theoretic Perception Grammar Hypotheses and Predictions' (L1 word-stress background), p. 135
5531.idn: Name in the source: Dhopadhola; family in the source: southern Luo language; Western Nilotic branch of the Nilo-Saharan language family

tn.quote: Dhopadhola has two underlying level tones (tonemes): High (H) and Low (L) according to Kaplan (2007). The only contour tones in Dhopadhola are falling tones (HL and H!H), and they only appear on a phonological phrase –final syllable and on syllables with long vowels. CVN syllables, (where N is a nasal) appear word internally, and other closed syllables appear only word finally. Neither kind of closed syllable can host a contour tone. … Under certain conditions, a high tone may spread rightward to an adjacent low-toned syllable.
tn.cite: Ayieko, Gerry Otieno. 2013. The perception and learnability of English prosodic phonology by Luo speakers: a cross-linguistic experimental study. PhD thesis, Makerere University, Kampala (January 2013). hdl:10570/2752.
tn.locator: sec. 3.2.2 'Dhopadhola Segmental and Prosodic Phonology', p. 51
tn.note: Two level tones, High and Low (after Kaplan 2007); falling HL and H!H contours only phrase-finally or on long vowels; H spreads rightward; stress fixed on the root-initial syllable.
